content:
Just a quick post that I now finished everything up to chapter 9 (so roughly ~70% of the book?) at https://github.com/rkirov/analysis. That includes 6 missing exercises in Ch 8.5 that I am upstreaming now https://github.com/teorth/analysis/pull/478.

I will write a longer blog post about this, but I am really settling into the Claude<>Lean workflow like this:

  1. Read textbook section
  2. Read the corresponding .lean file
  3. Read exercise in Lean + check textbook hints
  4. Write proof sketch in lean comments (key here is to think before sending Claude)
  5. AI completes the proof (if stuck, jump in - this is very rare, Claude if given enough time it always succeeds so far)
  6. Read proof carefully - compare it to the sketch. Ask Claude to explain if it strayed from sketch and find refactor opportunities if too long. Mostly look at proof strategy (which intermediate results proved, which theorems used), don't read too much into line-by-line tactics.
  7. go back to 3. until all exercises are done for the chapter

I am losing some opportunity to practice writing Lean (wrestling with the compiler), but do a bunch of reading and refactoring the lean proof, which keeps me engaged with Lean. Probably, it is capping me at advanced but not expert level of Lean, but I find the tradeoff worth it, as I can go a lot faster and hope to finish the book soon.

One curious thing to note is 8.5.18, proving axiom of choice from one of the equivalent statements, is a bit trickier in Lean's type theory (as ZFC' axiom of choice is not an axiom but consequence of Classical.choice). Claude convinced me there is no way to do it without Classical.choice - https://github.com/rkirov/analysis/blob/main/analysis/Analysis/Section_8_5.lean#L1983-L1999 but I am not 100% certain.

Thanks for this! I have no idea why the last few exercises in 8.5 were missing, I must have somehow skipped over them when writing the companion.

Lean inserts Classical.choice in just about everything, including the law of the excluded middle and the axiom of unique choice. One could in principle create a version of Exercise 8.5.18 in the set theory of Chapter 3, but this would be a lot of effort (and be somewhat dissonant in Chapter 8, where one has been using Mathlib's version of set theory for several chapters). These sorts of hidden uses of Classical.choice to prove the axiom of choice are I think OK for human students at least, who will be able to understand the spirit of the problem; it's possible that an AI attempting this exercise may find some way to solve it on a technicality, but that's a very minor issue all things considered.

Also, just finished a big rebase on top of current upstream main. One nice by product the verso build started working again (it was broken previously) and one can read the verso version of the proofs at https://rkirov.github.io/analysis
